what: highlight "Pricing of oil in US dollars: currencies used as a unit of account to price oil in the international market."
said: Not yen, not rupees, not euros. Dollars. Even when no American is part of the deal at all.

what: highlight "could be converted to gold at a fixed exchange rate of $35 per ounce"
said: Other countries could trade their dollars to the United States for gold, at thirty-five dollars an ounce.

what: highlight "owned over half the world's official gold reserves"
said: At first, this seemed rock solid. At the end of the war, America owned more than half of all the official gold in the world.

what: highlight "574 million ounces at the end of World War II"
said: That was five hundred seventy-four million ounces of gold. A mountain of metal, mostly sitting in vaults like Fort Knox.

what: highlight "of which only $3.2 billion was available to cover foreign holdings"
said: By the early nineteen seventies, foreigners held far more dollars than America had gold to give them. Only about three billion dollars of gold was really available to cover all those foreign dollars.

what: highlight "In March 1968, the London Gold Pool collapsed."
said: The cracks were already showing. In March nineteen sixty-eight, a group of central banks that had been holding the gold price steady in London gave up.

what: highlight "sent a ship to New York City to retrieve French gold deposits"
said: Other countries noticed. In August nineteen seventy-one, France even sent a ship to New York to bring its gold home.

what: highlight "Britain requested $3 billion in gold be moved from Fort Knox"
said: Days later, Britain asked for three billion dollars in gold to be moved from Fort Knox.

what: highlight "In 1971, President Nixon cancelled the fixed-rate convertibility of US dollars to gold ."
said: So on August fifteenth, nineteen seventy-one, President Nixon shut the gold window. Dollars could no longer be traded for gold.

what: highlight "effectively devaluing it by 7.9%"
said: A few months later, America tried a fix. It set a new official gold price of thirty-eight dollars, which cut the dollar's value by almost eight percent. It did not hold for long.

what: highlight "The petrodollar system originated in the early 1970s in the wake of the Bretton Woods collapse."
said: Now the dollar was just paper, backed only by trust in America. Nixon and his top diplomat, Henry Kissinger, worried the world might stop wanting dollars.

what: highlight "declared an oil embargo on the United States and the Netherlands"
said: In October nineteen seventy-three, war broke out in the Middle East. Several Arab oil producers, led by Saudi Arabia, stopped selling oil to the United States.

what: highlight "made the US economy vulnerable to a foreign oil embargo"
said: America had become dependent on foreign oil. Its own production was falling, and its economy ran on gasoline and diesel.

what: highlight "Richard Nixon requested $2.2 billion to support Israel's war effort"
said: The embargo followed America's decision to send two point two billion dollars to support Israel in that war.

what: highlight "from US$3/barrel to nearly US$12/barrel globally"
said: By March nineteen seventy-four, the price of oil had jumped nearly three hundred percent. From about three dollars a barrel to nearly twelve.

what: highlight "a national maximum speed limit of 55 mph"
said: Americans waited in long lines at gas stations. To save fuel, the government even set a national speed limit of fifty-five miles per hour.

what: highlight "Development of the Strategic Petroleum Reserve began in 1975"
said: The government also started building a giant emergency stockpile of oil in nineteen seventy-five, and created a whole new Department of Energy in nineteen seventy-seven.

what: highlight "generated the most diplomatic hostility the Saudi-U.S. relationship had seen thus far"
said: For Saudi Arabia, it was a turning point. The embargo caused the most tension the Saudi and American governments had ever had.

what: highlight "The 1973 embargo later came to be referred to as the first oil shock ."
said: For Saudi Arabia, it was a turning point. The embargo caused the most tension the Saudi and American governments had ever had.

what: highlight "The term petrodollar was coined in the early 1970s during the oil crisis"
said: These oil earnings got a nickname. Petrodollars. The word was coined in the early nineteen seventies, during the oil crisis.

what: highlight "the total current account surplus for all members of OPEC amounted to US$450 billion"
said: From nineteen seventy-four through nineteen eighty-one, the oil countries of OPEC built up four hundred fifty billion dollars in surpluses. That was an enormous amount at the time.

what: highlight "agreed that America would provide military protection for Saudi Arabia's oil fields"
said: America would protect Saudi Arabia and its oil fields. In return, Saudi Arabia would price its oil in US dollars.

what: highlight "A key part of the agreement was for Saudi to price oil in terms of dollars, and to invest billions of its dollars in U.S. Treasury notes."
said: And there was a second piece. Saudi Arabia would invest billions of its oil dollars in US Treasury notes. In other words, it would lend that money back to the American government.

what: highlight "Petrodollar recycling is the international spending or investment of a country's revenues"
said: Economists call this circle petrodollar recycling. The money leaves, and then much of it comes home.

what: highlight "were invested directly in U.S. Treasury securities"
said: Huge amounts of these Arab oil dollars went straight into Treasury securities, often handled quietly by government investment funds.

what: highlight "Especially during the years 1974–1981 and 2005–2014"
said: And it happened again, decades later. When oil prices stayed high from two thousand five to two thousand fourteen, oil countries piled up another wave of petrodollars.

what: highlight "OPEC oil is generally quoted in US dollars"
said: After these agreements, OPEC oil has generally been quoted in US dollars ever since.

what: highlight "an agreement to send Saudi Arabia 60 fighter jets"
said: The relationship also came with weapons. One deal included sending sixty American fighter jets to Saudi Arabia.

what: highlight "the United States dollar had become the world's dominant reserve currency"
said: By the middle of the twentieth century, the dollar had become the world's main reserve currency. Oil helped keep it there.

what: highlight "It was the Spanish silver dollar , however, which created the first true global reserve currency"
said: The dollar is not the first world money, by the way. Hundreds of years ago, the Spanish silver dollar played that role across Europe, Asia and the Americas.

what: highlight "made up less than 30% of global reserves"
said: Before World War Two, gold was still the main thing central banks held. Foreign money like the pound made up less than a third of their reserves.

what: highlight "it caused problems especially for oil-importing countries that were paying much higher prices for oil"
said: For countries that had to import oil, the nineteen seventies were brutal. They paid much higher prices, and many ran up big debts.

what: highlight "The international monetary system is facing its most difficult period since the 1930s."
said: The head of the International Monetary Fund said in nineteen seventy-four that the world's money system faced its hardest time since the nineteen thirties.

what: highlight "called the Oil Facility"
said: The IMF even set up a special lending program, called the Oil Facility, to help countries pay their oil bills.

what: highlight "exploits developing nations while advancing American imperialism"
said: Critics argue the whole system has favored America at the expense of poorer nations.

what: highlight "contributed to the bloc's collapse in 1989"
said: Oil money also shaped history in surprising ways. High oil prices helped the Soviet Union prop up its allies. When prices crashed in the nineteen eighties, that support fell apart.

what: highlight "Since the beginning of 2003, Iran has required payment in euros"
said: Some countries have tried to break away. Since two thousand three, Iran has asked for euros for many of its oil exports.

what: highlight "Venezuela joined the group of countries that allow their oil to be purchased in currencies other than US dollars"
said: In twenty eighteen, Venezuela started allowing its oil to be bought in euros, Chinese yuan and other currencies.

what: highlight "its share has declined over two decades"
said: The dollar's share of world reserves has also slowly slipped over the last twenty years, as central banks spread their savings into other currencies.

what: highlight "greatly limited OPEC's ability to control oil prices"
said: America itself changed too. Starting in the two thousands, the shale oil boom made the United States a giant oil producer again.

what: highlight "it took many years after the United States overtook the United Kingdom as the world's largest economy"
said: History shows this. Even after America became the world's biggest economy, it took many years for the dollar to replace the British pound as the main reserve currency.
